idiom_name: Play with Deadbolt 2 constraints (@SubjectPresent, @Restrict(@Group("admin"))) via a DeadboltHandler; plain Play ActionRefiner/ActionBuilder for a hand-rolled check
implementation_notes: The Scala/Play realization is Deadbolt 2: you supply a DeadboltHandler whose getSubject resolves the authenticated Subject (with its roles, permissions and restrictions), then annotate controller actions or templates with constraints - @SubjectPresent to require any subject, @Restrict(@Group("pauser")) or @Restrict(@Role(...)) to require role membership, and dynamic constraints for relationship rules; a denied request is routed to the handler's onAuthFailure (typically 403). Deadbolt is the decision layer and the constraint annotation is the enforcement seam. Without Deadbolt the same effect is a composed action: an ActionRefiner[Request, UserRequest] that resolves the user's roles and either returns a Forbidden Result or passes a refined request downstream (Play's documented ActionFunction/ActionBuilder composition), chained into a base controller so every endpoint inherits it. Roles are data in the application database; the Subject is built from it per request (cached) and never from client input. Spring Security's method security also applies from Scala on the JVM when the stack is Spring rather than Play.
pitfalls: An action without a Deadbolt constraint is open; constraints are opt-in per action, so centralize a base controller or a default constraint instead of trusting each author.
getSubject runs per request; an uncached database lookup on every action is the usual performance trap - cache per request or session.
Roles baked into a Subject at login go stale; a role revoked mid-session stays effective until the Subject is rebuilt.
A template constraint that disagrees with the controller constraint shows an action the endpoint then rejects (or hides a permitted one); keep one source of truth.
A custom ActionRefiner that fails open on an unexpected error (a Result path with no check) turns a lookup failure into access; default to Forbidden.
